title: Just Touch the Fingerprint Sensor to Summon AI: Pricing for Meta's New Palm-Sized Hardware Leaked

content_html:
Meta has moved the entry point for AI from the phone screen into your pocket. According to The Information on November 20, the palm-sized AI device Muse Charm that Mark Zuckerberg showed off in September is priced at about $300, or roughly RMB 2,008, and comes with up to 12 months of Verizon 5G data, so it can connect to the cloud anytime even without Wi-Fi.

One touch of a fingerprint bypasses the whole phone-unlocking process

Muse Charm's specs are quite restrained: an approximately 2-inch small screen displays the user's customized Muse avatar, while the real interaction trigger is hidden in the fingerprint sensor. With a touch of a finger, the device immediately starts a voice conversation—no need to unlock a phone or open an app—and you can talk directly with the Muse agent. Meta's intent is easy to read: compress "summoning AI" into a single touch and seize the interaction entry point before users open a phone app.

As for why the price has not yet been announced, the report says there may still be changes before its launch in the December holiday shopping season. Meta spokesperson Taylor Yi gave only a vague response, saying Meta welcomes outside attention and that more information would be shared "soon."

Open source keeps developers, smartwatch makes way for it

Meta is also betting on two fronts: first, the Muse Gadgets project open-sourced in October this year provides ESP32 and Linux SDKs, so developers can use a Raspberry Pi or ESP32 development board, hook up a screen, buttons, and sensors, and build their own terminal that connects to Muse; second, its originally planned smartwatch has been delayed to 2027 to prioritize getting Muse Charm to market on schedule.
